vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: vikunja-task-api
Version: 2.5.0

The vikunja-task-api skill is a legitimate integration for the Vikunja task management system. It provides a comprehensive set of API wrappers via the `vikunja.sh` bash script and detailed usage instructions in `SKILL.md`. The skill uses standard tools like `curl` and `jq` to interact with a user-defined Vikunja instance and requires standard API authentication (token or credentials). No evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or harmful prompt injection was found; the instructions provided to the AI agent are consistent with the stated purpose of managing tasks and projects.

llm.summary: The skill's files, instructions, and requested environment variables are consistent with a Vikunja API helper: it only needs a Vikunja URL and token (or username/password), uses curl/jq, and the included shell helper implements the same endpoints described in the documentation.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (Vikunja v2 API integration) matches the requested binaries (curl, jq), required VIKUNJA_URL, and primary credential VIKUNJA_TOKEN. The provided vikunja.sh implements the endpoints and flows documented in SKILL.md (login fallback, project/task endpoints). One minor metadata inconsistency: _meta.json / metadata lists VIKUNJA_TOKEN under optionalEnv while primaryEnv is set to VIKUNJA_TOKEN — practically the token is required for normal operation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md gives concrete installation steps and runtime examples that are scoped to Vikunja (API endpoints, how to set VIKUNJA_URL/VIKUNJA_TOKEN or username/password). It instructs storing credentials in ~/.openclaw/workspace/secure/api-fillin.env which is a plausible secure-location for this platform. There are no instructions to read unrelated system files, scan the host, or send data to unexpected external endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no external download/install spec. The only runtime code is the included shell script (vikunja.sh). No remote archives, URL shorteners, or arbitrary code downloads are present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The environment variables requested (VIKUNJA_URL plus VIKUNJA_TOKEN or fallback VIKUNJA_USERNAME/VIKUNJA_PASSWORD) are proportionate to a Vikunja API integration. Note the metadata inconsistency where VIKUNJA_TOKEN appears under optionalEnv even though primaryEnv is VIKUNJA_TOKEN; in practice the token (or username/password) is needed. SKILL.md also asks to store the token in a secure workspace file — expected for an automation skill but users should confirm that file is handled securely.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request elevated or permanent platform-wide privileges. It does not modify other skills or system configurations. Autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default) but not combined with other red flags.

dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: a thin CLI/instruction wrapper around your Vikunja server. Before installing: (1) Verify you trust the Vikunja server address you will set in VIKUNJA_URL. (2) Create a dedicated API token in Vikunja with minimal needed scope and store it in the secure workspace file the SKILL.md recommends (do not paste tokens into public chat). (3) Note the small metadata inconsistency about VIKUNJA_TOKEN being listed as optional in metadata — treat the token as required or provide username/password fallback. (4) Inspect vikunja.sh (provided) yourself if you have concerns; it uses only curl/jq and the official API paths. (5) If you later remove the skill, revoke or rotate the API token to avoid lingering access.
